newsitem.title: USA: Real estate transfer tax bill goes to Ill. gov..
newsitem.headline: Real estate transfer tax bill goes to Ill. gov..

text.p: A bill that would restrict the power of home-rule counties and municipalities in Illinois to increase or create a real estate transfer tax is headed to the desk of Gov. Jim Edgar.
The Illinois Senate overwhelmingly approved the bill Monday, following its passage Dec 5 in the House. The bill requires home-rule governments to hold a referendum to increase or create the tax.
A spokesman for Edgar said Tuesday the bill would be given a "thorough review."

The bill captured the spotlight late last year when an attempt was made by Cook County, the state's largest county, to increase its real estate transfer tax by 1,500 percent. County officials said the attempt, which fizzled out due to vocal public opposition, was aimed at beating final passage of the bill in the legislature.

Thomas Glaser, Cook County's chief financial officer, has also said that although rating agencies had no immediate concerns about the county's situation under the bill, there was a fear that such a constriction on revenue raising could lead to a rating downgrade.
